pr_title: LocalCache with read_multi should respect version and expire

issue_context.title: read_multi with ActiveSupport::LocalCache doesn't respect cache_version
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

When trying to use `Rails.cache.read_multi` when there's a local cache (like in a controller during a request, as set by the `LocalCache::Middleware`), it doesn't verify the cache version (check for `mismatched?`). I think it might also not check if the entry is expired.

This is a minimal script using a `MemCachedStore`, not sure if there's a quicker way to do it. I'm bumping the `cache_version` to reproduce, in my app I'm reproducing with an ActiveRecord object's `touch`.

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails"
  gem "dalli"
end

require "active_support"
require "minitest/autorun"

class Post
  attr_accessor :cache_version

  def to_param
    1
  end
end

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def test_using_a_local_cache
    cache = ActiveSupport::Cache.lookup_store(:mem_cache_store)
    cache.with_local_cache do
      post = Post.new
      post.cache_version = "001"
      key = ["foo", post]

      cache.write(key, "contents")

      assert_equal "contents", cache.read(key)
      assert_equal "contents", cache.read_multi(key)[key]

      post.cache_version = "002"
      assert_nil cache.read(key)
      assert_nil cache.read_multi(key)[key]
    end
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior

I'd expect `read_multi` to not return anything if the `cache_version` has changed. The test fails in the last line.

I could imagine that we use a local cache during a request so that cache reads are repeatable (sort of like an ActiveRecord query cache), but the behavior is inconsistent between `read` and `read_multi`, so I feel like it's a bug.

I can also see that [`read`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.0.1/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache.rb#L507-L513) has explicit checks for `expired?` and `mismatched?`, but [`read_multi`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.0.1/activesupport/lib/active_support/cache.rb#L536-L548) doesn't.

### Actual behavior

`read_multi` returns "stale" cache contents from the local cache.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 8.0.1

**Ruby version**: 3.4.1
